PMID:41104036.topic: Soft tissue knee injury pathway timescales and MRI use
PMID:41104036.setting: Acute knee clinic, Ashford and St Peter's Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (single NHS trust)
PMID:41104036.standard: NHS Constitution RTT standard (92% of consultant-led pathways completed within 18 weeks); Diagnostics DM01 standard (<1% waiting over six weeks for MRI); BOA/BOAST and regional MSK guidance of MRI within two weeks where diagnosis uncertain, with review within 7-14 days; NICE CKS and EBI guidance on selective MRI

cycle1.result: MRI utilisation 77.7% (269/346). Median waits: presentation to knee clinic 7 days, MRI referral to scan 33 days, scan to review 22 days; median presentation to diagnosis 60 days and to definitive management 97 days. 58.0% waited over four weeks for MRI; only 11.9% scanned within one week; 10.3% reviewed within seven days and 26.2% within 14 days. 42.8% of MRIs normal/degenerative.

PMID:41104036.other_findings: Surgery in 11.0% (38/346) with median 128 days from presentation to operation; only 7.2% of non-operative patients started physiotherapy within 30 days of clinic (median 70.5 days). GP referrals had longer median time to diagnosis (74 days) than UTC (53.5) or ED (58); a physiotherapy-first, criteria-based MRI pathway and re-audit were proposed.

PMID:39169647.topic: Fibreglass backslab offloading for plantar foot ulcers
PMID:39169647.setting: Multidisciplinary Diabetes Foot Unit and Podiatry clinics, Fiona Stanley Hospital, Perth (tertiary hospital)

cycle1.result: 28 patients (29 ulcers); 19 patients (20 ulcers) continued the backslab device. At 12 weeks median ulcer area 0.25 (0-0.55) cm2 with median reduction 97 (80-100)%; 9 (45%) ulcers completely healed (median 71 days) and 11 (55%) achieved at least 50% reduction (median 24 days).

PMID:39169647.other_findings: Nine patients (31%) stopped the device (irritation, discomfort, non-compliance, change of offloading, lost to follow-up); no device complications were documented in those who used it.

PMID:39757087.topic: Long-term survival of cross-arch stabilising bridges in periodontitis
PMID:39757087.setting: Specialist periodontal private practice, Egersund (rural referral practice)

cycle1.dates: Bridges constructed 1986 to 2016; observed up to 35 years
cycle1.result: 111 bridges in 94 patients; 16 bridges (14.4%) failed after 16.1 years (SD 4.0). Abutment tooth loss 8.9% vs 34.4% from the rest of the same arch and 25.4% from the opposing arch (p < 0.0001). Failure associated with poor oral hygiene (p = 0.0093) and complications during maintenance (p = 0.0059).

PMID:39757087.other_findings: Bridges with distal cantilevers failed in 16% and tooth-implant combination bridges in 14.0%; patients reported good satisfaction. Abstract gives 98 patients but the text reports 94.

PMID:35256273.topic: COVID-19 green pathway infection and mortality in foot and ankle surgery
PMID:35256273.setting: 46 NHS centres performing foot and ankle surgery (UK-FAlCoN national audit)

cycle1.dates: Phase 1: 13 January 2020 to 31 July 2020; Phase 2: 1 September 2020 to 30 November 2020
cycle1.result: Perioperative COVID-19 infection 1.07% (69/6470) on blue pathways vs 0.21% (9/4271) on green pathways (P < .001). No significant difference in phase 1; in phase 2 green pathway infection 0.16% vs 2.14% (OR 0.077). 30-day mortality 0.54% blue vs 0.09% green (p < .001); no difference in COVID-19-related mortality.

PMID:35256273.other_findings: COVID-19-related mortality fell from 25.71% (9/35) in phase 1 to 4.65% (2/43) in phase 2 (p = .008). Elective patients on green pathways rose from 49.73% to 90.83% between phases.

PMID:41446480.setting: Princess Royal University Hospital, Orpington (district general hospital, King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust)

cycle1.result: Incidence 1.32% (56/4,247 vaginal deliveries). Emergency response activated in 98.2% (mean response 2.3 minutes); McRoberts plus suprapubic pressure first line in 80.4%; internal manoeuvres in 37.5%; mean head-to-body delivery after recognition 4.7 minutes. Maternal complications 53.6%, PPH 7.1%; neonatal complications 83.9%, resuscitation 26.8%, NICU 3.6%, no permanent brachial plexus injury.

PMID:41446480.other_findings: 30.4% of cases had no identifiable risk factor; third/fourth degree tears in 7.1% and transient brachial plexus palsy in 3.6%. Better documentation systems and longer follow-up were recommended.

PMID:37529330.topic: Non-surgical biomechanical device for knee osteoarthritis
PMID:37529330.setting: Circle Integrated Care MSK service, Bedfordshire (NHS community musculoskeletal pathway)

cycle1.result: 65 (11.4%) referred for secondary care consultation over mean follow-up 3.5 years (mean 480.9 days to referral). WOMAC pain fell 43.2% (56.4 to 32.0 at 3 years), function improved 41.2%, OKS rose from 21.9 to 28.3 at 12 months and gait velocity rose 24.8% (all p < 0.05).

PMID:37529330.other_findings: 48% of referrals occurred in year 1 and 32% in year 2; there was no control group and actual knee replacement rates were not confirmed.

PMID:41640708.topic: Whole-body CT yield and radiation dose in trauma
PMID:41640708.setting: Seven Ministry of Health radiology departments (national multicentre)
PMID:41640708.standard: American College of Radiology guidelines for major blunt trauma

cycle1.result: 578 (42.3%) whole-body CTs negative and 789 (57.7%) positive, with 530 (38.8%) major injuries. Mean effective dose 19.98 ± 10.26 mSv for negative scans and 22.41 ± 10.35 mSv for positive scans.

PMID:41640708.other_findings: Road traffic accidents were 66.6% of referrals; fall from height had a higher positive rate. Clinical decision tools, dose monitoring and a national trauma registry were recommended.

PMID:34670774.topic: Enhanced recovery for shoulder arthroplasty length of stay
PMID:34670774.setting: Derby Shoulder Unit, University Hospitals of Derby and Burton NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Pre-enhanced recovery: mean LOS 2.38 nights, median 2 nights, single night stay rate 40.2%; complication rate 9.9%.

PMID:34670774.intervention: Enhanced recovery programme via PDSA cycles: MDT-led preoperative class with OT home assessment, new patient information booklet and DVD, standardised anaesthetic/analgesic protocol with carbohydrate and gabapentin loading, and a physiotherapy protocol with sling for comfort only and early safe-zone mobilisation.

cycle2.dates: 6 October 2017 pilot; full roll-out 7 December 2017 to 8 October 2018
cycle2.result: Matched enhanced recovery cohort: mean LOS 1.89 nights (median 2), single night stay rate 49.2%; 15 fewer bed nights; complication rate 7%; OSS and Constant scores similar at 3 and 12 months.

PMID:34670774.other_findings: Adherence to dexamethasone use was only 36% (80% on re-audit of 15 patients) and gabapentin compliance only 24%; 12 patients had discharge delays because social services would not accept pre-admission referral.

PMID:26734416.setting: Trauma unit, Ulster Hospital, Dundonald (district general hospital)
PMID:26734416.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England handover guidance (2007) plus local orthopaedic-specific criteria

cycle1.result: Poor handover: patient location 57%, responsible consultant 14%, results of significant/pending investigations 29%, co-morbidities 38%, outstanding tasks 38%; one patient not handed over and one nerve injury not handed over.

PMID:26734416.intervention: Trauma-specific paper handover proforma (SHOs informed by email and verbally), then an electronic proforma accessible from any hospital computer, created with IT.

cycle2.result: With the electronic proforma only one criterion fell below 95% (results of pending investigations 82%); no patient safety issues; proforma uptake 100%.

PMID:26734416.other_findings: Intermediate re-audit with the paper proforma (10/02/15 to 16/02/15, 19 patients in text, 17 in abstract): management plan 76%, results of investigations 47%, outstanding tasks 71%, all other criteria at least 80%.
